title: What If You Traveled at 99.9999% the Speed of Light?
alt_titles: What You'd See at 99.9999% the Speed of Light
What If You Flew at 99.9999% Light Speed?
description:
What would you actually see, feel and survive if you traveled at 99.9999% of the speed of light? We turn the dial one nine at a time, from 10% to 99.9999%, with a real star catalog bent by relativity on screen.

In this video:
• Why the whole sky collapses into one patch ahead of you, and why the famous starbow ring is a myth
• How fast your clock runs compared to Earth's at every speed
• Which speed turns empty space into a lethal radiation beam
• What each extra nine costs in energy
• How far you could really get in one lifetime, and what you'd come home to

⏱ Chapters
0:00 The Sky at 99.9999%
0:16 The Ship and the Dial
1:08 10%: Nothing Feels Different
2:17 50%: The Sky Starts Sliding
3:29 90%: The Speed That Kills
4:52 99%: Half the Universe in a Circle
5:33 99.9%: The Stars Ahead Fade
6:11 99.99%: The Starbow Myth
7:11 99.9999%: One Year, 707 Years
8:35 Beyond: The Andromeda Trip
9:33 Coming Home

🧮 Key numbers
• At 99.9999% of light speed: 1 year on board = 707 years on Earth
• At 90%: each hydrogen atom carries 1.21 GeV; unshielded, a lethal dose in under half a second
• At 99.99%: half the sky fits in a circle 1.6° wide, and the cosmic microwave background ahead reaches 385 K
• Energy for an ISS-mass ship at 99.9999%: about 45,000 years of world energy use
• 1 g ship to Andromeda: 28.6 years on board; round trip 57 years for you, 5 million years on Earth

Assumptions: an ISS-mass ship cruising at a fixed speed (energy is the minimum, perfect engine, no fuel); typical interstellar gas of about 1 hydrogen atom per cm³; dose figures are unshielded lower bounds; the Andromeda trip uses constant 1 g acceleration with a midpoint flip.

How this was made: the narration is an AI voice (text-to-speech) and the script and visuals are made with AI tools and code. Every number is computed in code from the sources above and fact-checked before upload.
